meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Pointing at something. Core Russian part meaning 'here, there (pointing)' in everyday speech.
Emphasis. Core Russian part meaning 'here, there (pointing)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: 'вспомни' = remember (that) . Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'помнить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to remember, to recall', paired with 'вспоминать'.

examples.text: Я этого не хочу. Но вспомни, у тебя сын болеет.
examples.trans: I don't want that. But remember, your son is ill.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.
Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.

related.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'wife' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'm with my wife this evening.

examples.text: Но вечером я обещал быть с женой.
examples.trans: But I promised to be with my wife this evening.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: A fact or a person. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'вестный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('famous, well-known').

examples.text: Он самый известный человек в городе.
examples.trans: He is the most famous man in town.

examples.text: Вы сами подумайте. Он самый известный человек в Синеозерске!
examples.trans: Think about it yourselves. He is the most famous man in Sineozersk!

examples.text: Он самый известный человек в Синеозерске!
examples.trans: He is the most famous man in Sineozersk!

meanings.note: Predicative: очень интересно. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Как интересно!. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Как интересно! А в Москве ты про меня гадости рассказываешь.
examples.trans: How interesting! And in Moscow you go around saying nasty things about me.

meanings.note: In questions. Core Russian det meaning 'what; what a' in everyday speech.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: in the instrumental: 'кем ты работаешь?'

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: A very polite request. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('kind, polite').

meanings.en: 'Будьте любезны' = would you be so kind
meanings.note: A very polite request. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('kind, polite').

examples.trans: Would you be so kind as to call me.

examples.text: Генерал Круглов ждёт звонка. Будьте любезны.
examples.trans: General Kruglov is waiting for a call. If you'd be so kind.

meanings.note: + infinitive. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: кого + instrumental: назвать меня плохим словом
Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'звать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to call, to name', paired with 'называть'.

examples.trans: You called me a bad word.
What will you name your son?

examples.text: Ты назвал меня плохим словом. Меня, начальника!
examples.trans: You called me a bad word. Me, your boss!

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
hesitation, at the start of a sentence
Ну, папа!. Core Russian part meaning 'well; come on' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
For masculine and neuter things. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.
Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'куда').

examples.trans: Where does that word come from?
Thief, thief. Where does that word come from?

отойти.gloss: to step back, to move away

meanings.en: to step aside, to move back
meanings.note: Perfective of отходить. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'ойти'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to step back, to move away', paired with 'отходить'.

examples.trans: He stepped over to the window.
Step back! No comment! No comment!

meanings.note: С первого раза = the first time. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('first').

examples.text: Ты не понимаешь с первого раза?
examples.trans: You don't understand the first time?

examples.text: Ты что, с первого раза не понимаешь?
examples.trans: What, you don't understand the first time?

meanings.en: to try, to have a go
meanings.note: + infinitive. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пробовать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to try', paired with 'пробовать'.
Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пробовать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to try', paired with 'пробовать'.

examples.text: Как я могу это забыть? Ну, давай попробуем.
examples.trans: How can I forget that? Well, let's try.

meanings.note: очень похоже = that's just like him
Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'хоже').

examples.text: Правда похоже. А может, вы сами позвоните губернатору?
examples.trans: It really is. Why don't you call the governor yourself?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'прашивать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to ask', paired with 'спросить'.

examples.text: Вот это что такое, я вас спрашиваю!
examples.trans: What is this, I'm asking you!

meanings.note: To someone you call ты. Core Russian det meaning 'your (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: At that time. Core Russian adv meaning 'then, back then' in everyday speech.
Core Russian adv meaning 'then, back then' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: Agent noun formed with the international suffix '-ист' denoting a specialist or adherent. Common masculine noun meaning 'footballer, soccer player' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The money is with the footballer now.

examples.text: Твои деньги сейчас у футболиста Магиди.
examples.trans: Your money is with the footballer Magidi right now.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.
